items.title: Well-founded recursion gives a function whose value depends on the values at smaller arguments
items.author: The Univalent Foundations Program
items.work: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics

items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 10.3.7 at source lines 1009-1016: given a set B, a function g from the power set of B to B and a well-founded relation < on A, there is f:A->B with f(a)=g(setof{ f(a') | a'<a }) for every a:A. The author's proof (source lines 1019-1029) is short but its whole content is a single careful recursion: one has to recurse on the accessibility witness rather than on the element of A, supplying at each step not only the values fbar(a',s(a')) but the witnesses s(a') for the predecessors, and only then discharge the accessibility hypothesis through the well-foundedness of < to obtain a genuine function on A. The statement records the recursion equation but neither the accessibility recursion nor the passage from fbar to f.
